state.question: Assess Inland Stores's reported inventory service level. I need the following measured result: September order-line fill rate from stock and the change from August on the same customer cohort.
state.conclusion: Inland increased safety stocks at its regional depot.
state.gap: September order-line fill rate from stock and the change from August on the same customer cohort.

candidates.title: Inland Stores: what the announcement changes
candidates.abstract: I set out the case for Inland Stores's strategy in inventory service level, using incentives and managerial judgement to project the next stage.

candidates.title: Inland Stores: the strategic argument
candidates.abstract: Our reporting desk follows Inland Stores, drawing on an independent correspondent's account of september order-line fill rate from stock and the change from August on the same customer cohort.

candidates.title: Inland Stores: the measurement desk
candidates.abstract: Inland order-line ledger supports a dated assessment of september order-line fill rate from stock and the change from August on the same customer cohort.

candidates.title: Inland Stores: the operating record
candidates.abstract: An edited digest of Idris Kwan's Dispatch's dispatch on Inland Stores, retaining its reported comparison and attribution.

candidates.title: Inland Stores: the weekly notebook
candidates.abstract: Inland Stores features in a field guide to inventory service level. The worked example draws on a separate setting: a finance newsletter discusses stock-market fills for limit orders.

candidates.title: Inland Stores: the latest field dispatch
candidates.abstract: A commentary revisiting Inland Stores's operating announcement, carrying the same factual account as the public record.
